## Business Entry Reform Project Phase II Launched

GIS News Headline News 16 July 2015 Hits: 2106

ImageThe Ministry of Justice, Immigration and National Security is partnering with the World Bank Group to implement Phase II of the Business Entry Reform Project.

In June 2014, the World Bank Group welcomed the opportunity to partner with the Government of Dominica to implement Phase II of the project, seeking to enhance and upgrade Dominica’s online registration system, thereby helping businesses to become operational more quickly.

The idea is to create an integrated "one stop shop" for the local business community, with an electronic platform that will streamline a variety of procedures, including social security registration, commercial registries, operating licenses and tax registries.

In Phase I of the Business Entry Reform Project, the Companies and Intellectual Properties Office (CIPO), which is responsible for administering laws, the registration and preservation of records relating to intellectual property, companies, business names and international business companies in Dominica, transitioned from a manual system to a new e-registry and online company registration software in November 2012.

The project improved the operations of the CIPO by streamlining the legal framework for business/company registration, providing a new harmonized electronic system for registering companies and business names and establishing an electronic connection between the CIPO and tax and social security authorities.

 Since then in excess of 409 new companies were incorporated and 1,150 businesses names registered.

Phase II of the Business Entry Reform Project was launched on Wednesday, July 15, 2015.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
